subject: MedicLaim MAP: hosting path, evaluation milestones, and timeline
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@mediclaim.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluation map and hosting questions

Hi Laura — thanks for the intro call today. As discussed, our execs want a clear mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out: evaluation cadence, acceptance criteria for PoC, and the target production hosting choice (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with a recommended region for initial rollout.

Key constraints: data residency for a subset of PHI-like documents, a hard SLA requirement for 99.9% availability once in production, and cost targets relative to our current inference spend. Can you send a draft MAP and a short evaluation timeline we can review with Procurement?

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Integrations, MedicLaim Health
Alicia.Gomez@mediclaim.com

Attachment: none
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@mediclaim.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MedicLaim MAP: hosting path, evaluation milestones, and timeline

Hi Alicia — great to follow up. I’m attaching a draft MAP (MedicLaim_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) and an initial 4-week evaluation plan. High level recommendation from our side:

- PoC (2–4 weeks): use Redwood Hosted to validate integration, latency, and model quality quickly. Hosted minimizes onboarding friction and lets us run controlled A/Bs.
- Prod target (after PoC): Dedicated capacity if you need predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Private deployment is available for the regulated set of data with strict residency requirements.

Suggested evaluation milestones (week-by-week):
1) Week 0: integration + baseline telemetry (latency, token cost)
2) Week 1: model quality run with stability tests and prefix caching enablement
3) Week 2: load test for 95/99th latency and batching config tuning
4) Week 3: compliance/security checklist and go/no-go decision

Next steps: can Karthik take point on the technical acceptance criteria and Marissa on the commercial milestones? I’ll fold Procurement into the next update.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: MedicLaim_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@mediclaim.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: MedicLaim MAP: hosting path, evaluation milestones, and timeline

Thanks Laura — looping in a couple technical points that will influence hosting choice:

- Data residency slice: if MedicLaim requires on-prem or single-region hosting for the PHI subset, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the right option for that slice. For general inference traffic we can route to Hosted or Dedicated in the US-east region.
- Performance: we’ll need peak qps and median/99th latency targets to size Dedicated pools. Can you share expected concurrent sessions and avg seq length?
- Features: KV cache prefixing and model quantization profiles (4-bit quant) reduce unit cost but affect quality trade-offs — we should include a short eval matrix in the MAP.

Alicia — can Procurement share the SLA and retention requirements? I’ll prepare a technical acceptance checklist and a dedicated-sizing estimate.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: procurement@mediclaim.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: MedicLaim MAP: hosting path, evaluation milestones, and timeline

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the overview. A few items Procurement needs documented before we can sign off on a MAP: 
1) SOC 2 / security evidence and a timeline for shared attestation
2) Long-term cost estimate (12-month committed for Dedicated) vs Hosted baseline
3) Data retention and deletion guarantees for the PHI-like documents in the Private footprint

I attached a short RFP_response.xlsx with the fields we need populated. Please return the completed sheet and a one-page summary of the Dedicated SLA (uptime, maintenance window policy, incident response).

Best,
MedicLaim Procurement Team
procurement@mediclaim.com

Attachment: RFP_response.xlsx

Subject: Re: MedicLaim MAP: hosting path, evaluation milestones, and timeline

Hi Procurement / Alicia — attached is an updated MAP workbook (mutual_action_plan_mediclaim_v2.xlsx) that populates the RFP fields at a high level and includes:

- Link to our SOC 2 Type II report and our security onboarding checklist (see Drive link below).
- 12-month committed Dedicated estimate (ballpark) vs Hosted pay-as-you-go baseline — line items included for GPU hours, storage, and network egress.
- Data residency and deletion: we offer separate Private tenancy for the PHI subset with customer-managed keys (KMS) and documented retention deletion SLA (30 days for cached KV, configurable retention for logs).

Proposed dates for the MAP:
- Start PoC: 2026-11-22
- Interim technical review: 2026-12-06
- Go/no-go decision: 2026-12-20

I also added a short acceptance criteria table (quality thresholds, latency targets, and throughput). Link to HubSpot MAP: https://hubspot.company/contacts/HLTH-3241

If that looks good, Marissa will prepare a commercial sketch and I’ll schedule a security pre-call with your team.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks, that’s helpful. We accept the proposed MAP dates and milestones. Request one small add: can we add a 30–45 minute security pre-call the week of 11/15 to validate SOC evidence and key rotation? Otherwise, we’ll plan to start PoC on 11/22.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alicia
